subject: Dedicated capacity sizing for DeepBurst pilot - telemetry & burst clarifications
messages:
From: Elena Cruz <elena@deepburst.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing: DeepBurst pilot (Q4)

Hi Marcus / Marissa,

Thanks again for taking the time today. As discussed, DeepBurst is planning a Q4 pilot to move inference onto a dedicated Redwood fleet. We collected a quick telemetry snapshot from our staging cluster and attached it (deepburst-telemetry-snapshot.csv). High-level requirements:

- Baseline concurrent sessions: ~1,800 (avg over business hours)
- Peak concurrent sessions during marketing spikes: up to 5,500 for 3-8 minute windows (rare, ~15 times/day)
- P95 latency target: 250ms for standard chat flows (typical prompt ~40 tokens, typical response ~220 tokens)
- Long-generation tail: ~18% of requests exceed 1k tokens (these are async/codegen jobs)
- KV / prefix caching: we have per-user prefix reuse for 35% of sessions (large benefit when warm)
- Burst pattern: concentrated US PST 09:00-17:00 with two repeat spikes 11:00 and 15:00 PST

Questions for sizing:
1) Do you need raw request traces, or the CSV snapshot is sufficient for an initial sizing proposal?
2) How do you recommend we model the long-generation tail for canary vs. steady-state capacity?
3) Any specific guidance on cache warmers or pre-warming strategies we should run during the pilot?

We need an initial committed capacity number and an outline of the canary rollout plan by next week.

Attaching: deepburst-telemetry-snapshot.csv (5MB, truncated)

Thanks,
Elena Cruz
Head of ML Ops
DeepBurst Technologies
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena@deepburst.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing: DeepBurst pilot (Q4)

Elena — thanks for the snapshot and the clear ask. Quick answers up front, then a short set of clarifying questions so we can produce a defensible committed footprint:

Short answers:
- CSV snapshot looks useful for an initial dimensioning. Raw traces help refine batching estimates but aren’t strictly required for a first pass.
- For the long-generation tail we usually model as a separate async pool (smaller throughput, higher per-request GPU-time). Canary should start with an elevated tail fraction to validate autoscaling triggers.
- Cache warmers: we can provide a warming script and recommend a 20–30 minute pre-warm window before business-hour ramps.

Clarifying questions:
1) When you say \"concurrent sessions,\" is that concurrent websocket sessions (affects KV cache) or concurrent in-flight inference requests? If both, please break out numbers.
2) Do the long-generation requests accept best-effort P95 >1s, or do they require the same 250ms target?
3) What model family are you planning to serve on Redwood (open Llama- style, /gpt-family equivalent, or a custom fork)? That affects memory + KV cache sizing.
4) Are you open to a hybrid routing policy (short-chat to low-latency variants, long-gen to throughput-optimized quantized variants)?

I put together a draft SLO/footprint workbook and a couple of sample prompt/response snippets to help estimate tokens-per-request and batching behavior — attaching burst-slo-draft.xlsx and sample-prompts-and-responses.txt.

If you can confirm the three clarifications above and upload an hourly request time-series (or just the CSV with timestamps bucketed to 1m), we’ll turn around an initial dedicated sizing and a canary matrix.

Proposed next step: 30-min call tomorrow to align on model family and tail requirements; I’ll invite Karthik for the capacity simulation.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: burst-slo-draft.xlsx (workbook with baseline/canary scenarios)

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing: DeepBurst pilot (Q4)

Marcus — thanks for the quick turnaround and the workbook. Quick clarifications below and I pasted two representative prompt/response pairs at the end.

Breakouts:
- Concurrent websocket sessions (active user sessions holding KV state): baseline 1,800; peak 5,500.
- Concurrent in-flight inference requests (stateless): baseline 2,200; peak 6,400 (during the 5,500 session spikes some users trigger background inference jobs).

Tail SLA:
- Long-generation (>1k tokens) can accept higher latency; target for that class is P95 <2.5s. Short-chat SLA must meet the 250ms P95.

Model family:
- We plan to use an LLaMA-derivative we maintain internally (parameters ~13B, we will provide the model binary).
- We are open to hybrid routing (short-chat to an optimized quantized variant, long-gen to a full-precision variant) if Redwood supports automatic fallback.

Cache behavior:
- Per-user KV prefix reuse: ~35% warm. Prefetching is possible if we provide a list of high-frequency users beforehand.

Traffic shape:
- Day-of-week: Mon-Fri concentrated, Sat minimal.
- Spikes typically last 3–8 minutes and correlate with marketing triggers.

Links: HubSpot deal  DB-4891 (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/DB-4891). I uploaded a 1m-bucketed CSV to your shared Drive folder.

   Response: ~312 tokens (contains lists and numbered items)

Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity sizing: DeepBurst pilot (Q4) — initial sizing proposal and action items

Team — forwarding the thread and pulling together an initial proposal so we can lock a committed capacity recommendation for the pilot. Summary and proposed plan below. (Forwarded message included)

Summary (from ELENA):
- Baseline concurrent sessions: 1,800 websocket sessions; baseline in-flight requests ~2,200
- Peak concurrent sessions: up to 5,500; peak in-flight requests up to 6,400 during marketing spikes
- Short-chat target: P95 <250ms; long-gen target: P95 <2.5s
- Model: customer-provided LLaMA-derivative (~13B); cache reuse ~35% when warm

Marcus’s initial sizing hypothesis (ballpark):
- Committed baseline fleet: equivalent of 12 large-GPU workers (approx. 12 x A100-80GB class) to handle baseline tokens with conservative batching estimates and 35% cache hit;
- Burst buffer / autoscale headroom: additional on-demand capacity to cover spikes up to 6,400 in-flight requests (suggest 4–8 extra workers depending on quantization option and routing).
- Tail pool: dedicated 2-3 throughput-optimized workers for >1k token jobs to keep long-gen jobs from impacting short-chat latency.
- Canary plan: stage 4 GPUs (small canary) for 48–72 hours with increased tail fraction enabled; if stable, ramp to 50% of committed baseline for 24 hours, then to 100%.
- Cache warmers: run 30-minute pre-warm before morning ramp; provide prefetcher for top 10% heavy users.

Action items:
1) Marissa — please draft the reserved-capacity pricing for the baseline 12-worker commit + autoscale headroom options and one-time canary engineering time. Target ETA EOD 2026-12-02.
2) Karthik — run a capacity simulation using the 1m-bucketed CSV on the model config (13B, approx memory/kv footprint in workbook). Provide a sensitivity table showing required workers vs. assumed batching (tokens-per-batch) by 2026-12-03.
3) Monica — prepare the operational runbook for cache warmers and the canary rollout (include rollback triggers and telemetry signals).
4) Marcus — I’ll coordinate the call with Elena to align on hybrid routing and confirm whether they will accept quantized variants for short-chat.

Notes: This is an initial hypothesis — we should expect 10–20% deltas once Karthik runs the sim with real traces and once we test model memory behavior.

Thanks — let’s treat this as time-sensitive given the Q4 pilot start window.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
